msContents.summary: Collection of tracts in Latin and Italian by various hands. This section is written in a neat humanistic hand, 30 lines to a page: headings in red. [li](Anon.) Ars memoriae artificialis: Fol. 1 (red) Tractatus breuis et solemnis scientiam et ad conse/quendam artem memoriae artificialis ad illustrem/Marchionem mantuae missus feliciter incipit.//[I]Ussu tuo princeps illustissime artifica/lis memoriae regulas... (Text begins) [P]RAECEPTORE Cicerone/ac enim teste sancto thoma... 16 ... quos mihi comparaui. uale diu et/feliciter princeps illustrissime./M.CCCC.LIX.[/li][li](Anon.) Tractatus solemnis aris memorativae: Fol. 17 (red) Tractatus sollemnis artis memoratiue incipit./[A]RTIFICLOSAE memoriae egregia quedam/atue preclarissma precepta... 20, line 8 ... cum eius mente/notare ut fuerit (Table) Anello. Erba. 20v (End of table) 70. Quaglia. 100 Giouane famelglio.[/li][li]Girardus, Magister. Ars memoriae. (By Balduinus Sabaudiensis?): Fol. 21 (red) Tractatus artis mimoratiue eximii doctoris/artium et medicine domini magistri giradi./[A]RS commoda naturae confiramat et auget ut inquit/egregius tullius... 25, line 7 Intersissa [sic] perit continuata uiget. FINIS.[/li][li]Cicero (M. T.). De oratore, (Extract): Fol. 25, line 8 (red) M. T. CICERONIS IN LIBRO DE ORATO/re haec de memoria scripta sunt./[H]ABETIS de inueniendis rebus disponendisque/... 26, line 23 sed cret si latet euocanda est.[/li][li]Cicero (M. T.). Rhetoricorum ad C. Herennium. (Extract): Fol. 26v, line 24 (red) M. T. CICERO IN HIO. RHETORICORVM/artificialem memoriam suctiliter [sic] docuit./[M]EMORIA utrum hebeat quicquid artificiosi... 30v ... et quod maxime necesse/est exerciatatone confirma. tos. PERVSIE.//(red) FINIS.[/li][li]Gonzaga (Guido da). Leggenda di S. Clemente: Ff. 31-74 Cominza la istoria di santo clemente in vulgare translatato/per guido da gonzaga protonotario.[/li][li](Gonzaga (Guido de).) Leggenda di S. Silvestro: Ff. 75-96 [D]apoy la morte dicclationo [sic] et magiminao [sic] imperatori di roma... These two tracts are written in an early 16th century current hand. Ff. 97-99 Blank.[/li][li]Extacts from the Proceedings of the Venetian Senate: Ff. 100-126 on commercial affairs from 1508 to 1649, compiled by various 16th/17th century hands: in Italian. 127-130 Blank. Fol. 131 Table of Contents for the remainder of the volume. 132 Blank.[/li][li]Albertus Magnus, St. Semita recta: followed by some alchemical receipts: Written in an early 16th century semi-current italic hand. Fol. 133 Ihesus christus marie filius sit mihi in hoc opus propitius./Incipit liber domini Alberti [this has been written in over the original 'Io[hann]is Roberti'] super Alchimiam.//Omnis sapientia a domino deo est... 154 ...Et/hoc est elixir quod transmutat omnia metalla in solem/et in lunam in una hora. Ff. 154v-157 Alchemical receipts: In Latin and Italian.[/li][li]Rupescissa (J. de). De consideration quintae essentiae. (Incomplete): Written by an early 16th century hand. Ff. 158, 159 Blank. Fol. 160 Incipit liber de consideratione 5ae essentiae omnium/transmutabilium et est liber de familiatu philosophie euangelicis contem/plantibus viris et pauperibus.//[D]Icit Salomon in libro. sapientie. capitulo, vii. Deus dedit... . 183 Remedium xxm ut in spasmo generatur febris.../.../expertiex eis quod is succo flama/.[/li][li](Synesius.) Oneirocriticon: in Latin: Written by a late 16th century hand. Fol. 184[/li][li](Anon.) Sermons, etc: in Latin, the last in Italian: Ff. 188-199 written in a late 16th century hand. 200-201 Blank.[/li][li](Rusio (Lorenzo)?). Collection of veterinary receipts: Ff. 202-213 in Italian: Perhaps from the 'Liber mareschalciae equorum'. They are bound in wrong order: Caps. 193-204, 135-192, 75-122, and include many charms and incantations. By a late 16th century hand.[/li][li]Miscellaneous medical, household and technical receipts: Ff. 214-228 in Latin or Italian by various hands of the first half of the 17th century: some written on single sheets. Fol. 223 contains a note on a coin of Otho, apparently addressed to M. Rainssant [ -1689] Directeur des Médailes a Versailles. Ff. 226, 227 contain a receipt in Italian, but written in Greek characters, for 'IIot ipaic i uiov pxeiv'.[/li][li](Anon.) Regole di aritmetica per rispondere a quesiti: Ff. 229-263 A treatise on fortune telling by letters and numbers, with tables.[/li]

objectDesc.supportDesc: 1 volume1 l. + 264 ff. 4to. 21 1/2 x 15 cm. 18th century vellum binding, with flower-pattern end-papers. some margins frayed. The beginning and end of the Collection of veterinary receipts (No. 13) are wanting, and the leaves are bound in wrong order. The first 5 items, which apparently from one original tract, are on paper of smaller format (21 1/2 x 14 1/2 cm.).
